newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 31.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page March 31:

CINCINNATI - Of all the family stories behind the 39 neatly strewn corpses discovered in the rooms of a Southern California mansion last week, perhaps none is more unsettling than that of a working mother named Yvonne McCurdy-Hill.

PHILADELPHIA - Handsomely arrayed against the backdrop of Boston's historic Faneuil Hall and the city's Liberty Bell, the settings could not have been more auspicious for the launching of a drive "to renew American democracy" by overhauling its widely abused campaign financing system.
MOSCOW - A powerful few rule the Russian mass media where financial and political clans reap profits and gain influence.
WASHINGTON - Forty area families search for housing and help as D.C. Village, the city nursing home that has served as a wider shelter for the homeless, prepares to close.

TOKYO - In what may be a first in trans-Pacific economic relations, the United States is targeting the power of a single individual who heads the Japan Harbor Transportation Association -- the effective boss of the country's 50,000 dockworkers -- in demanding changes at Japanese ports.

WASHINGTON - Across Washington and the country, chain stores better known for lingerie, chicken sandwiches and decaf lattes are aggressively hawking music, setting up their own recording labels, selling millions of albums and giving traditional record shops new competition.
